Low hard sun rakes in from the left almost parallel to the sand; hot amber against indigo shadow; one blown-white specular runs the full length of the cut face of the near wall; every shovel-scrape holds its own black.

Backlight from directly behind the tallest tower; the near faces go cadmium-orange at the edges, deep violet everywhere else; one rim of fire traces the tower's upper curve; the trench between the two walls unreadable.
Sun so low it comes from behind the structure; every top edge is trimmed in brass; the wet sand throws back cold blue-grey; the undersides of the turrets go almost black.

Storm light: a bruise-purple band across the sky with one break of hot yellow lying across the wet sand exactly where the towers rise; the structure at the far side edge of the frame drops into purple.
Blue hour, the wet sand still holding the last of the orange against a field of deep cold blue; one hard specular line traces the notched top of the wall; the dry sand behind stays slate.

Low sun through thin sea mist; the air itself turns gold and the shadows stretching from every ridge go indigo; a single hot line runs across the wet sand where the water laps; the far turrets dissolve into the indigo.
A flat pearl sky; the wet sand reads as deep slate; the only committed warmth in the frame is the painted edge of the one plastic tool half-buried in the near wall; every scrape around it stays cold.
Hard low sidelight from the right; the notched top of the wall becomes a row of black teeth against a field of hot ochre; the flanks of the turrets glow brass; the trench goes dark.

Sun so low it arrives from beneath the crest of the near wall; the underside of every overhang is lit rose-gold while everything above it sits in cold blue-grey; the sand right beneath the crest glows copper.
Rose dawn light from the water side; the foam on its lit face reads pink, on its shadow face slate; that rose catches the near tower's upper curve; the dry sand behind stays cold violet.

Green-gold light bounced up from bright wet sand into the shaded undersides of the turrets; the tops stay deep indigo; the illuminated undersides carry a colour not seen from above; the dry sand behind reads dark amber.
A narrow band of hot tangerine light crossing the sand exactly where the towers stand, both sides of that band falling into cool grey-blue; the towers are lit, the ground around them extinguished.

Deep teal fills every shadow; brass light skims only the very tops of the walls, leaving the faces below in cold dark; the one highlight is a hard brass line along the ridge of the highest wall; the trench goes black.

Moonlight-cold silver on the wet sand, every ridge throwing a long blue-white shadow; one patch of amber low on the near wall where the dry sand is still releasing the day's stored heat; the far towers vanish into silver-grey.
Cloud shadow covers most of the frame; one hard sunlit stripe of cadmium yellow crosses the canal and the two walls flanking it; everything outside that stripe falls into deep violet-grey.

Low sun from the water side, almost horizontal; the wet sand throws every grain of it back as gold against the cold grey of the dry sand; the one specular runs the wet face of the near wall; the far face stays dark.

Backlight low and left; every top edge of the structure catches fire in hot orange while the near faces sink to near-black; the long shadow of the tallest tower crosses the frame in deep blue-violet; the trench is unreadable.

Late gold pressing in from the right so low the turrets cast shadows ten times their own height across the sand; cold cobalt sits in every scrape and notch; the specular is a single gold line along the wall's ridge; the bases go black.

Sun exactly behind the tallest tower, flaring round its upper curve in a ring of hot white-gold; the lit sand each side reads cobalt in comparison; the tower's near face is nearly black; the specular runs only the upper curve's edge.

Low raking light from the far side, amber against the deep indigo of the near faces; the wet sand at the base of the structure returns the amber as a narrow bright strip; the insides of every cut go black.

Hard low sidelight turning every ridge into a blade; the lit faces burn in raw sienna, the shadow faces drop to cold slate; the one hard highlight rides the top of the dam's near corner; the interior of the structure is darkness.

Rose and copper dawn light from low left, the long shadow of each turret running cobalt blue across the dry sand; the cut face of the near wall carries one blown specular of white-gold; the shadow faces stay deep violet.

Sun at last light almost behind the structure; the wet sand in front lights up in brass against the far field of deep blue-grey; the one specular runs the entire near edge of the wall; the turrets are dark silhouettes.

Thin high overcast breaking along the bright water band; a single concentrated band of hot lemon light reaches the sand at a very low angle; the shadows it throws are long and indigo; the dry sand catching none of it stays cold grey-blue.

Low backlight through sea mist; the mist layers the air in stacked gold and the shadows beneath each ridge go deep indigo; the tallest tower's rim carries a continuous hot line; every scrape in the sand holds its own dark.
